data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 frames the central relation as a *covering principle* — simultaneous compatibility (with SRC_003) and contradiction (with SRC_005) — but the refutation condition it proposes does not actually test that principle. It refutes only if the produced answer falls outside x≡18 (mod 35), a condition that fails to discriminate the two levels it relies on (method vs. correctness). An answer like 53 is in the progression and would pass the refutation guard, yet 53 is the very value that *simultaneously* triggers method-compatibility with SRC_003 and answer-correctness contradiction with SRC_005 — i.e., the same case the target endorses. So the refutation admits an instance of the asserted relation while also permitting an instance that breaks it (e.g., 88 shares the mechanism but is not the minimal answer, so it should contradict SRC_005 the same way). By the covering-principle stance, the relation must be stable across the entire progression the target names, but SRC_001 only secures membership, not the compatibility/contradiction split it advertises.
